subject.title: refactor: move MCP OAuth state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw accept the immediate Doctor-only cutover for existing MCP OAuth credentials, with no runtime fallback, once live fresh-install and upgrade proof is attached?
rationale: The change intentionally makes credential availability depend on a one-time operator migration and moves bearer retry ownership across a security-sensitive dependency boundary; tests cannot establish that this upgrade and authorization policy is the intended release contract.

options.title: Approve after live proof
options.body: Accept the single-store design after redacted fresh-login, legacy-upgrade, refresh, logout, restart, and reauthorization evidence confirms the full user path.

options.title: Require migration UX first
options.body: Hold the cutover until the release provides a more visible in-product or startup-guided Doctor recovery path for installations that still have legacy credentials.

options.title: Defer the storage migration
options.body: Keep the existing file-backed runtime for this release and revisit the SQLite transition with a separately approved rollout plan.

recommendation.title: Approve after live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the single-store design after redacted fresh-login, legacy-upgrade, refresh, logout, restart, and reauthorization evidence confirms the full user path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available recent MCP/runtime contributor and authored the paired migration direction.
